title: The First World War

cards.h: A wrong turn in Sarajevo lit a fuse across the world
cards.b:
On 28 June 1914, the Austrian heir, Archduke Franz Ferdinand, was driving through Sarajevo. His car stalled after an earlier bomb attempt failed. A 19-year-old named Gavrilo Princip was standing nearby. He shot the Archduke and his wife.

Within six weeks, Europe was at war.
Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia. Alliances pulled in Russia, Germany, France and Britain. Germany's plan was to knock out France fast. It failed, and the armies dug in.

From late 1914 the Western Front was a line of trenches from the sea to Switzerland. Machine guns made charging deadly. On 1 July 1916, the first day of the Somme, Britain suffered about 57,000 casualties, with about 19,000 killed.

New horrors: poison gas (used at Ypres in 1915), tanks (1916), aircraft and submarines.

cards.h: A truce and a long war
cards.b:
At Christmas 1914, soldiers on parts of the front stopped firing and swapped gifts. It was short-lived and not general.

In 1917 the US joined after German submarine attacks, while Russia, torn by revolution, left the war. Germany asked for an armistice, which began on 11 November 1918.

Roughly 9-10 million soldiers died, plus millions of civilians. Four empires fell: German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman. The Treaty of Versailles (1919) blamed Germany and imposed reparations.

The 1918-19 influenza pandemic, helped by troop movements, killed many more.

After the war, Germany was blamed. In 1961 Fritz Fischer argued Germany pushed for war. In 2012 Christopher Clark's The Sleepwalkers argued all powers stumbled into it.

A famous myth: soldiers were 'lions led by donkeys'. Historians now say that image is too simple, since commanders learned and tactics improved.

Five things to remember

  1. The war began after Sarajevo in 1914.
  2. Trench warfare killed millions.
  3. Ended on 11 November 1918.
  4. Four empires collapsed.
  5. Indians served in large numbers.

Think about it

  • Why did alliances make a local crisis global?
  • What did India get for its sacrifice?
